title: Minimal Insights telemetry slice: scope trims, acceptance criteria, and decision log
creator: Aisha Patel
body:
Context: The Console Insights initiative must deliver a minimal telemetry surface that gives product and platform engineers actionable signals about request latency, error rates, and per-route cost drivers without delaying the initial MVP launch. Prior attempts to include full tracing, per-token flamegraphs and long-retention raw logs increased scope and schedule risk. This ticket defines the scoped MVP slice, rationale for exclusions, and concrete acceptance criteria so engineering and design have a single source of truth for the upcoming cycle.

Scope_included (MVP slice):
- Top-level dashboards: 3 cards (Aggregate throughput & latencies; Error rate + top error types; Cost per route - top 10 routes).
- Sampling-based tracing: 1% probabilistic sampling for traces, surfaced as a lightweight trace list linked from the error card (no full-span waterfall UI).
- Cost breakdown: per-route token estimate shown for top 10 routes across the selected time window; estimate uses current pricing model and token-metering export (approximate, +/-10%).
- Alerting hooks: webhook-able thresholds for latency P95 and error rate (to integrate with existing alerting infra).
- Basic query filters: time window, region, and model variant.

Out_of_scope (MVP cut):
- Full trace waterfall UI with span-level inspection (deferred).
- Per-token flamegraphs and top-k expensive tokens (deferred).
- Long-term raw trace retention >30 days (deferred to a later launch).
- Per-customer chargeback and multi-tenant cost allocation (post-MVP).
- Advanced rollups (e.g., per-customer daily aggregation) beyond top-10 route surface.

Rationale for cuts:
- Tracing waterfall and span inspection add significant UI/infra work and require storage/retention design that risks slipping the release by multiple sprints. Lightweight sampled traces give immediate debugging utility for high-impact errors while keeping storage bounded.
- Full per-token analysis and flamegraphs are high-cost to compute and store; initial cost breakdown driven by top-10 routes will capture >85% of observed spend in customer telemetry based on historical usage.

Design and engineering constraints:
- Dashboard cards must render within 300ms for default queries (SLO).
- Sampling pipeline should use existing trace-client sampling knobs; collected traces stored in the ephemeral traces store with 30-day TTL.
- Cost calculation must be explainable: include a tooltip showing assumptions (pricing per token, rounding, sample window).

Stakeholders: ["Aisha Patel <aisha@redwood.com>", "Rafael Gomez <rafael@redwood.com>", "Mira Chen (Design) <mira@redwood.com>", "Anika Rao (Observability) <anika@redwood.com>"]

Links: ["PRD: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/IN/Console+Insights+PRD", "Design mockups V1: https://drive.redwood.com/designs/console-insights-v1", "Token-metering export spec: https://github.com/redwood/telemetry/blob/main/token-metering.md", "Existing parent initiative: PM-41258"]

Notes: The product team discussed this slice with Eng and Design on 2026-03-09. Eng flagged two backend unknowns (query latency for large time windows, and cost-estimation accuracy when using sampled traces). This ticket includes proposed mitigations and follow-ups in follow_up_tasks.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard: Aggregate throughput & latency card shows total requests, P50, P95, P99 latency and updates within 5 minutes of ingestion for default 1h window
Dashboard: Error card lists top 5 error types by count and includes a link to view sampled traces for a selected error group

Dashboard: Cost per route card lists top 10 routes by estimated spend and shows unit assumptions in tooltip (pricing per token and sample rate). Values within +/-10% of offline batch estimate for the same window
Tracing: Sampled trace list is available from error card and returns trace metadata (trace id, latency, route, error flag) for sampled traces within selected window
Alerting hooks: Webhook delivery for threshold breaches is sent for latency P95 and error rate and is visible in console alert history
Performance: Dashboard default queries render within 300ms median and 95th percentile under 1.5s in staging
Docs: PRD and user-facing short help copy are published before release and linked from the dashboard
decisions: 1) Keep tracing minimal: 1% probabilistic sampling; defer span-level UI -> reduces storage and UI scope
2) Cost surface limited to top-10 routes by spend to reduce computation; justify via data showing these routes cover majority of spend
3) Retention capped at 30 days for traces in MVP to control infra costs
4) No per-customer chargeback in MVP; provide export hooks for downstream billing systems instead
open_questions: Q1: Is 1% sampling sufficient to capture rare, high-impact errors? (Eng to run sampling-sensitivity analysis by 2026-03-18)
Q2: Should cost estimates use sampled token counts scaled up or rely on token-metering export? (Decision: use metering export when available, fallback to scaled sampling)
Q3: Do we need a throttle on dashboard query complexity (e.g., limit long-window aggregation)? (TBD with infra team)
Q4: Which roles get access to cost card by default in the Console RBAC model? (PM to propose default access)
follow_up_tasks: PM-46901: sampling-sensitivity-analysis (Eng) - run simulation on 60-day historical data to validate 1% sampling capture rate
ENG-18014: optimize-dashboard-query-paths - add query-time bounding and pre-aggregations for top metrics
ENG-18042: implement-trace-ttl-and-storage-limits - ensure traces auto-expire at 30 days
DES-1012: mockups-and-copy - finalize microcopy for cost assumptions tooltip and alerting flows
testing_notes: Test plan: use synthetic workload to validate cost estimates against offline batch calculation, verify sampled trace surfacing for known injected errors, and run perf tests on staging with 100k requests/hour to validate query SLOs. Include manual verification steps for tooltip copy and alert delivery in slack/webhook endpoints.
implementation_risks: Risk: cost estimates may diverge for routes with highly variable token usage; mitigation: include explanation in UI and provide export for customers to reconcile. Risk: 1% sampling may miss extremely rare concurrency bugs; mitigation: add higher-probability sampling for error responses and provide on-demand debug sampling toggle for critical customers.
notes_history: 2026-03-09: Kickoff with Eng+Design; agreed on top-10 routes cut. 2026-03-11: Eng requested deferral of span UI due to infra backlog. 2026-03-13: PM proposed alerting hooks as MVP add - accepted. 2026-03-14: Updated acceptance criteria to include performance SLOs and docs requirement.
